problem_markdown: For every integer $n\ge3$, construct $n$ plane points with all pairwise distances irrational and every three forming a nondegenerate triangle of rational area.
solutions_markdown:
Take $P_j=(j,j^2)$ for $j=1,\ldots,n$. For $j>i$,
$$P_iP_j=(j-i)\sqrt{1+(i+j)^2}.$$
The integer under the square root lies strictly between $(i+j)^2$ and $(i+j+1)^2$, so it is not a square and its square root is irrational. Multiplying by the nonzero integer $j-i$ preserves irrationality.

For $i<j<k$, the determinant area formula gives
$$[P_iP_jP_k]=\frac{(j-i)(k-i)(k-j)}2.$$
This is positive and rational. Thus the construction has both required properties.
